an10.29:1.1: (1) “Bhikkhus, as far as Kāsi and Kosala extend, as far as the realm of King Pasenadi of Kosala extends, there King Pasenadi of Kosala ranks as the foremost.
an10.29:1.2: But even for King Pasenadi there is alteration; there is change.
an10.29:1.3: Seeing this thus, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with it;
an10.29:1.4: being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate toward the foremost, not to speak of what is inferior.
an10.29:2.1: (2) “Bhikkhus, as far as sun and moon revolve and light up the quarters with their brightness, so far the thousandfold world system extends. In that thousandfold world system there are a thousand moons,
an10.29:2.2: a thousand suns, a thousand Sinerus king of mountains, a thousand Jambudīpas, a thousand Aparagoyānas, a thousand Uttarakurus, a thousand Pubbavidehas, and a thousand four great oceans; a thousand four great kings, a thousand heavens ruled by the four great kings, a thousand Tāvatiṁsa heavens, a thousand Yāma heavens, a thousand Tusita heavens, a thousand heavens of devas who delight in creation, a thousand heavens of devas who control what is created by others, a thousand brahmā worlds.
an10.29:2.3: As far, bhikkhus, as this thousandfold world system extends, Mahābrahmā there ranks as the foremost.
an10.29:2.4: But even for Mahābrahmā there is alteration; there is change.
an10.29:2.5: Seeing this thus, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with it;
an10.29:2.6: being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate toward the foremost, not to speak of what is inferior.
an10.29:3.1: (3) “There comes a time, bhikkhus, when this world dissolves.
an10.29:3.2: When the world is dissolving, beings for the most part migrate to the devas of streaming radiance.
an10.29:3.3: There they exist mind-made, feeding on rapture, self-luminous, moving through the skies, living in glory, and they remain thus for a very long time.
an10.29:3.4: When the world is dissolving, the devas of streaming radiance rank as the foremost.
an10.29:3.5: But even for these devas there is alteration; there is change.
an10.29:3.6: Seeing this thus, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with it;
an10.29:3.7: being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate toward the foremost, not to speak of what is inferior.
an10.29:4.1: (4) “Bhikkhus, there are these ten kasiṇa bases.
an10.29:4.3: One person perceives the earth kasiṇa above, below, across, undivided, measureless.
an10.29:4.4: One person perceives the water kasiṇa …
an10.29:4.12: the consciousness kasiṇa above, below, across, undivided, measureless.
an10.29:4.13: These are the ten kasiṇa bases.
an10.29:5.1: Of these ten kasiṇa bases, this is the foremost, namely, when one perceives the consciousness kasiṇa above, below, across, undivided, measureless.
an10.29:5.2: There are beings who are percipient in such a way.
an10.29:5.3: But even for beings who are percipient in such a way there is alteration; there is change.
an10.29:5.4: Seeing this thus, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with it;
an10.29:5.5: being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate toward the foremost, not to speak of what is inferior.
an10.29:6.1: (5) “Bhikkhus, there are these eight bases of overcoming.
an10.29:6.3: i “One percipient of forms internally sees forms externally, limited, beautiful or ugly.
an10.29:6.4: Having overcome them, he is percipient thus: ‘I know, I see.’
an10.29:6.5: This is the first basis of overcoming.
an10.29:7.1: ii “One percipient of forms internally sees forms externally, measureless, beautiful or ugly.
an10.29:7.2: Having overcome them, he is percipient thus: ‘I know, I see.’
an10.29:7.3: This is the second basis of overcoming.
an10.29:8.1: iii “One not percipient of forms internally sees forms externally, limited, beautiful or ugly.
an10.29:8.2: Having overcome them, he is percipient thus: ‘I know, I see.’
an10.29:8.3: This is the third basis of overcoming.
an10.29:9.1: iv “One not percipient of forms internally sees forms externally, measureless, beautiful or ugly.
an10.29:9.2: Having overcome them, he is percipient thus: ‘I know, I see.’
an10.29:9.3: This is the fourth basis of overcoming.
an10.29:10.1: v “One not percipient of forms internally sees forms externally, blue ones, blue in color, with a blue hue, with a blue tint.
an10.29:10.2: Just as the flax flower is blue, blue in color, with a blue hue, with a blue tint, or just as Bārāṇasī cloth, smoothened on both sides, might be blue, blue in color, with a blue hue, with a blue tint,
an10.29:10.3: so too, one not percipient of forms internally sees forms externally, blue ones….
an10.29:10.4: Having overcome them, he is percipient thus: ‘I know, I see.’
an10.29:10.5: This is the fifth basis of overcoming.
an10.29:11.1: vi “One not percipient of forms internally sees forms externally, yellow ones, with a yellow hue, with a yellow tint.
an10.29:11.2: Just as the kaṇikāra flower is yellow, yellow in color, with a yellow hue, with a yellow tint, or just as Bārāṇasī cloth, smoothened on both sides, might be yellow, yellow in color, with a yellow hue, with a yellow tint,
an10.29:11.3: so too, one not percipient of forms internally sees forms externally, yellow ones….
an10.29:11.4: Having overcome them, he is percipient thus: ‘I know, I see.’
an10.29:11.5: This is the sixth basis of overcoming.
an10.29:12.1: vii “One not percipient of forms internally sees forms externally, red ones, with a red hue, with a red tint.
an10.29:12.2: Just as the bandhujīvaka flower is red, red in color, with a red hue, with a red tint, or just as Bārāṇasī cloth, smoothened on both sides, might be red, red in color with a red hue,
an10.29:12.3: with a red tint, so too, one not percipient of forms internally sees forms externally, red ones….
an10.29:12.4: Having overcome them, he is percipient thus: ‘I know, I see.’
an10.29:12.5: This is the seventh basis of overcoming.
an10.29:13.1: viii “One not percipient of forms internally sees forms externally, white ones, white in color, with a white hue, with a white tint.
an10.29:13.2: Just as the morning star is white, white in color, with a white hue, with a white tint, or just as Bārāṇasī cloth, smoothened on both sides, might be white, white in color, with a white hue, with a white tint,
an10.29:13.3: so too, one not percipient of forms internally sees forms externally, white ones….
an10.29:13.4: Having overcome them, he is percipient thus: ‘I know, I see.’
an10.29:13.5: This is the eighth basis of overcoming.
an10.29:13.6: “These are the eight bases of overcoming. Of these eight bases of overcoming,
an10.29:14.1: this is the foremost, namely, that one not percipient of forms internally sees forms externally, white ones, white in color with a white hue, with a white tint,
an10.29:14.2: and having overcome them, he is percipient thus: ‘I know, I see.’
an10.29:14.3: There are beings who are percipient in such a way.
an10.29:14.4: But even for beings who are percipient in such a way there is alteration; there is change.
an10.29:14.5: Seeing this thus, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with it;
an10.29:14.6: being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate toward the foremost, not to speak of what is inferior.
an10.29:15.1: (6) “Bhikkhus, there are these four modes of practice.
an10.29:15.3: Practice that is painful with sluggish direct knowledge;
an10.29:15.4: practice that is painful with quick direct knowledge;
an10.29:15.5: practice that is pleasant with sluggish direct knowledge;
an10.29:15.6: and practice that is pleasant with quick direct knowledge.
an10.29:15.7: These are the four modes of practice.
an10.29:16.1: Of these four modes of practice, this is the foremost, namely, practice that is pleasant with quick direct knowledge.
an10.29:16.2: There are beings who practice in such a way.
an10.29:16.3: But even for beings who practice in such a way there is alteration; there is change.
an10.29:16.4: Seeing this thus, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with it;
an10.29:16.5: being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate toward the foremost, not to speak of what is inferior.
an10.29:17.1: (7) “Bhikkhus, there are these four modes of perception.
an10.29:17.3: One person perceives what is limited;
an10.29:17.6: and still another, perceiving ‘There is nothing,’ perceives the base of nothingness.
an10.29:17.7: These are the four modes of perception.
an10.29:18.1: Of these four modes of perception, this is the foremost, namely, when, perceiving ‘There is nothing,’ one perceives the base of nothingness.
an10.29:18.2: There are beings who perceive in such a way.
an10.29:18.3: But even for beings who perceive in such a way there is alteration; there is change.
an10.29:18.4: Seeing this thus, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with it;
an10.29:18.5: being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate toward the foremost, not to speak of what is inferior.
an10.29:19.1: (8) “Bhikkhus, of the speculative views held by outsiders, this is the foremost, namely: ‘I might not be and it might not be mine; I shall not be, and it will not be mine.’
an10.29:19.2: For it can be expected that one who holds such a view will not be unrepelled by existence and will not be repelled by the cessation of existence.
an10.29:19.5: There are beings who hold such a view.
an10.29:19.6: But even for beings who hold such a view there is alteration; there is change.
an10.29:19.7: Seeing this thus, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with it;
an10.29:19.8: being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate toward the foremost, not to speak of what is inferior.
an10.29:20.1: (9) “Bhikkhus, there are some ascetics and brahmins who proclaim supreme purification. Of those who proclaim supreme purification,
an10.29:20.2: this is the foremost, namely, by completely surmounting the base of nothingness, one enters and dwells in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
an10.29:20.3: They teach their Dhamma for the direct knowledge and realization of this.
an10.29:20.4: There are beings who assert thus.
an10.29:20.5: But even for those who assert thus, there is alteration; there is change.
an10.29:20.6: Seeing this thus, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with it;
an10.29:20.7: being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate toward the foremost, not to speak of what is inferior.
an10.29:21.1: (10) “Bhikkhus, there are some ascetics and brahmins who proclaim supreme nibbāna in this very life. Of those who proclaim supreme nibbāna in this very life,
an10.29:21.2: this is the foremost, namely, emancipation through non-clinging after one has seen as they really are the origin and passing away, the gratification, danger, and escape in regard to the six bases for contact.
an10.29:21.3: “Bhikkhus, though I assert and declare my teaching in such a way, some ascetics and brahmins untruthfully, baselessly, falsely, and wrongly misrepresent me, by saying:
an10.29:21.4: ‘The ascetic Gotama does not proclaim the full understanding of sensual pleasures, the full understanding of forms, or the full understanding of feelings.’
an10.29:21.5: But, bhikkhus, I do proclaim the full understanding of sensual pleasures, the full understanding of forms, and the full understanding of feelings. In this very life, hungerless, quenched, and cooled, I proclaim final nibbāna through non-clinging.”
